=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: the `created_at <= $latch_created_at` provenance check inside `release_staged_support_needs_human_latches` (around the `_current_needs_human_event` jq predicate the LAST RUN DIFF shares a function with) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: GitHub timestamps have second-level precision. When the latest `ai:needs-human` `labeled` event and the staged-support latch comment share the same `created_at` second, the `<=` allows the latest event to be considered "before" the latch even when the relabel logically followed it; the actor check still passes because both came from the same trusted actor.
  WHY: a trusted actor who re-labels `ai:needs-human` immediately after creating the latch in the same second would have the same-second timestamp pair pass `<=`, the sweep would then treat the latest label event as belonging to the original latch instance, and could post `/approved` for a latch the actor just deliberately set. It is low-risk (the trusted actor already has direct label and `/approved` authority), but the contract is "the latest `ai:needs-human` event precedes the marker" and ties defeat it.
